summary_paragraph: A 34-year-old woman with sickle cell disease was admitted for a pain crisis affecting her knees, left hip, and right shoulder. She had been managing pain at home with oral and injectable Dilaudid, but increasing severity prompted her to seek emergency care. During her hospital stay, she received intravenous fluids and IV pain medication, leading to significant improvement. Imaging confirmed avascular necrosis in both femoral heads, worse on the right, with concern for early changes in the left hip. The orthopedic team evaluated her and recommended outpatient MRI and follow-up for potential future hip replacement. Her Hepatitis C with stage III fibrosis was noted, and her Hydroxyurea dose was reduced to 500 mg twice daily to balance efficacy and liver safety. She was discharged home in stable condition with a plan for ongoing pain management, specialist follow-up, and monitoring of her chronic conditions.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Aseptic necrosis of head and neck of femur
Pain in joint, pelvic region and thigh
